subject.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs

question: Should file-transfer policy formally interpret existing `~\...` entries as Windows home-relative globs, thereby activating previously non-matching allow and deny rules?
rationale: The code change is technically narrow and proven, but automation cannot decide whether reinterpreting stored file-access policy is an acceptable shipped compatibility and security-boundary change.

options.title: Accept Windows home syntax
options.body: Confirm `~\` as equivalent to `~/` for file-transfer policy and land the focused implementation with the demonstrated deny precedence.

options.title: Retain slash-only syntax
options.body: Keep the current contract and close or revise this PR if avoiding reinterpretation of existing stored policy is more important than Windows-native syntax.

recommendation.title: Accept Windows home syntax
recommendation.body: Confirm `~\` as equivalent to `~/` for file-transfer policy and land the focused implementation with the demonstrated deny precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical file-transfer implementation history shows this person directing its security hardening and landing path.
